scope_issue_assessments.detail: Radiographs provide alignment, avulsion and visible soft-tissue clues. Retained tendon/ligament and cartilage requirements need appropriate direct imaging or separately identified explanatory anatomy; normal clear spaces do not prove ligament integrity.
scope_issue_assessments.classification_note: The effective radiograph-first checklist explicitly distinguishes indirect injury clues from direct acquired soft-tissue imaging. The retained ligament/cartilage targets and all representation requirements remain unchanged.

scope_issue_assessments.detail: Foot/hindfoot and proximal-fibular findings apply only to actual acquired coverage; unexamined sites remain explicit requirements for the relevant pathway, not silently normal structures.
scope_issue_assessments.classification_note: The report explicitly records actual foot/hindfoot and proximal-fibular coverage. This conditional boundary does not waive required anatomy or permit an unexamined site to count as covered.

scope_issue_assessments.detail: The source uses distribution across multiple joint groups. A single hand, knee or generic joint cannot demonstrate symmetry, spared joints or the entire examination.
A normal regional bone mesh cannot resolve all possible host bones, tumour compartments or neurovascular relationships. Site selection and specialist-reviewed lesion representation remain required.

The source contains a sentence calling the lateral ulnar collateral ligament a tendon. The requirement correctly classifies it as ligament; source wording must not drive mesh tissue classification.
scope_issue_assessments.classification_note: The effective worksheet and requirement classify LUCL as a ligament. The inconsistent source sentence is a retained terminology boundary, not an unresolved runtime classification defect. Missing LUCL geometry and both required components remain unverified.

scope_issue_assessments.detail: Adult elbow bones do not depict age-specific physes and unossified cartilage. Radiographs cannot directly evidence cartilage continuity or clinical neurovascular normality. Dedicated paediatric representations remain required.
A native femur/acetabulum asset cannot satisfy implant component, liner, cement or zonal interface requirements.
Labrum, cartilage lesions and periarticular soft-tissue findings are conditional on an appropriate acquired MRI; do not attach those claims to a radiograph-only illustration.
scope_issue_assessments.classification_note: The effective checklist and worksheet already condition labral, cartilage-lesion and periarticular soft-tissue assessment on acquired MRI and preserve not-assessed states. This is a retained modality boundary, not a radiograph-only tissue-integrity claim; all anatomy and representation obligations remain.

scope_issue_assessments.detail: The older source emphasizes three posterolateral structures. The requested complete corner anatomy also decomposes smaller ligament/fascicle components; these expansions require current MSK specialist verification.
No single fixed muscle model can satisfy a site-dependent examination. The current required set remains unresolved until a named region-specific instance is enumerated.

Ultrasound cannot be counted as a complete substitute for all MRI labral sectors, deep articular cartilage or capsuloligamentous attachment assessment.

Clinical neurology is an external examination input. Direct ligament/neural assessment depends on the acquired MRI, while CT morphology and injury clues remain reportable. These limits persist after the scoped report correction.
scope_issue_assessments.classification_note: The dedicated trauma guide already separates CT morphology, acquired MRI assessment and supplied clinical neurology. The former inherited-report defect was corrected; level expansion and all neural/ligament targets remain required.
